claims.text: Treats: neomycin + polymyxin B cover S. aureus, E. coli, H. flu, Klebsiella-Enterobacter, Neisseria and P. aeruginosa (not Serratia or strep).
claims.quote: Neomycin sulfate and polymyxin B sulfate together are considered active against the following microorganisms: Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Klebsiella-Enterobacter species, Neisseria species, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This product does not provide adequate coverage against Serratia marcescens and streptococci, including Streptococcus pneumoniae.

claims.text: MOA: hydrocortisone (corticoid) suppresses the inflammatory response and may delay healing.
claims.quote: Corticoids suppress the inflammatory response to a variety of agents and they may delay healing.

claims.text: Know: for superficial bacterial infections of the external auditory canal (and mastoidectomy/fenestration cavities).
claims.quote: For the treatment of superficial bacterial infections of the external auditory canal caused by organisms susceptible to the action of the antibiotics, and for the treatment of infections of mastoidectomy and fenestration cavities caused by organisms susceptible to the antibiotics.

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to any component; herpes simplex, vaccinia and varicella infections.
claims.quote: This product is contraindicated in those individuals who have shown hypersensitivity to any of its components, and in herpes simplex, vaccinia, and varicella infections.

claims.text: Caution: neomycin can cause permanent sensorineural hearing loss (risk ↑ w prolonged use; limit to 10 days); don't use w a perforated TM.
claims.quote: Neomycin can induce permanent sensorineural hearing loss due to cochlear damage, mainly destruction of hair cells in the organ of Corti. The risk is greater with prolonged use. Therapy should be limited to 10 consecutive days (see ). Patients being treated with eardrops containing neomycin should be under close clinical observation. Neomycin and Polymyxin B Sulfates and Hydrocortisone Otic Suspension should not be used in any patient with a perforated tympanic membrane.

claims.text: Allergy: neomycin may cause cutaneous sensitization (low-grade redness, swelling, dry scaling, itching, or failure to heal); stop if it occurs.
claims.quote: The manifestation of sensitization to neomycin is usually a low-grade reddening with swelling, dry scaling, and itching; it may be manifest simply as a failure to heal. Periodic examination for such signs is advisable, and the patient should be told to discontinue the product if they are observed.

claims.text: Know: if not improved after 1 week, repeat cultures and susceptibility tests.
claims.quote: If the infection is not improved after 1 week, cultures and susceptibility tests should be repeated to verify the identity of the organism and to determine whether therapy should be changed.
